gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a MagSafe wallet with built-in Find My costs $36.99 on ESR's own US store (Geo Wallet Boost, 4 cards plus 3 bills, 1,800 g magnet hold), against $69 on Nomad's store for its Leather Mag Wallet Find My Tracking, which ChatGPT showed at $99. It also doesn't state that Smartish's own store sells the Side Hustle wallet for $24.99–$29.99 and the iPhone 17 Wallet Slayer Vol. 2 for $34.99.
standout_why: Of the rival pages, I could only read Macworld's Best iPhone 17 cases (cited). Its readable part has no wallet entries and no wallet prices, and the Bellroy 3 Card entry ChatGPT credited to it was in the truncated section. I couldn't open the other rival pages: Good Housekeeping (cited) and Esquire refused the fetch, and Wirecutter returned 403 through both nytimes.com and the proxy. So I can't rule out that one of them prints the ESR price. The price for Find My, set out across ESR, Nomad and Smartish from each maker's store today, isn't in anything I could read, and ChatGPT's own answer gave $99 for Nomad.
decides: It backs our page's lead pick, the ESR Geo Wallet Boost. It gives the same 4-card capacity and Find My as the Nomad at $36.99 against $69, and ChatGPT's $99 Nomad card looks out of date. For shoppers who want one piece, the maker-store price for the Smartish Wallet Slayer on iPhone 17 is $34.99 for Vol. 2, not the $29.99 ChatGPT showed for Vol. 1 at Best Buy. Our row still names Vol. 1, so it should be checked against what Smartish sells now.
